raw_response:
I am getting old now, so I do not fool around too much with new ways. On my 6 mu, I will still do wheat and then maize, same as before. This way is steady. If one season is not good, the other can still bring something back. I have only 2 people at home, and money is not loose, so I will use what I know worked in past years. I have a well, so if the sky does not give rain, I can still save the crop, but pumping water costs money, so I will not water too many times unless the land is really dry.

For wheat, I will sow in early October, not too late, or it does not tiller well before winter. I will use ordinary local wheat seed, the kind I can get nearby, not expensive fancy seed. Fertilizer, I will put most under before sowing, then add some urea later when the wheat starts standing up and growing fast. I do not dare use too little, because if wheat turns yellow, yield drops fast. For maize, once wheat is cut in June, I will hurry and plant right away. There is no time to waste between the two crops. I will use hybrid maize seed because maize seed now mostly comes that way and gives better ears. I will not do heavy tillage, just a quick field preparation and sow. If rain is decent, one irrigation may be enough for maize, but wheat I trust less to the weather, so I plan more water there.
